title: A geometric-point morphism gives an equivalence of pointed étale neighbourhoods
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let s : Spec k → S and s' : Spec k' → S be geometric points [def-weil-geometric-point]. For a scheme morphism a : Spec k → Spec k' satisfying a ≫ s' = s, precomposition with a gives an equivalence from the category of pointed étale neighbourhoods of s' to that of s [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], over the small étale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. On objects it sends (U,t) to (U,a ≫ t), and on arrows it preserves the underlying S-morphism.

proof.text: (Morphisms from the spectrum of a field.) For a field $K$ and a scheme $X$, by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] a morphism $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ is the same as a pair $(x,\varphi)$ of a point $x\in X$ and a field homomorphism $\varphi:\kappa(x)\to K$, via $g=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$, where $j_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ is the canonical morphism; write $g=(x,\varphi)$. Two rules follow. (i) If $h:X\to Y$ is a morphism and $r_x:\kappa(h(x))\to\kappa(x)$ the induced map of residue fields, then $h\circ(x,\varphi)=(h(x),\varphi\circ r_x)$: by [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] $h\circ j_x=j_{h(x)}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r_x)$, so $h\circ g=j_{h(x)}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r_x)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)=j_{h(x)}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi\circ r_x)$ ($\operatorname{Spec}$ is a contravariant functor [def-weil-affine-spectrum]), and the pair is read off by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field]. (ii) The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k'$ has a single point $\xi'$, whose residue field is $k'$ itself with $j_{\xi'}=\mathrm{id}$ (the field-spectrum identification, or directly Spec.homEquiv); hence by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] the morphism $a$ is $a=\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)$ for a unique field homomorphism $\alpha:k'\to k$, which is injective (a ring map between fields). For every $g=(x,\varphi):\operatorname{Spec}k'\to X$ we get $g\circ a=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha\circ\varphi)$, i.e. $g\circ a=(x,\alpha\circ\varphi)$. Consequently precomposition with $a$ is injective on morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to X$: if $(x_1,\alpha\circ\varphi_1)=(x_2,\alpha\circ\varphi_2)$ then $x_1=x_2$ and $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$ because $\alpha$ is injective.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Remark 04FN (remark-map-stalks, lines 3416-3441): 'the functor above is clearly an equivalence'; written out here

proof.text: (Lifts as field embeddings.) Write $\bar s'=(s,\beta')$ with $s\in S$ and $\beta':\kappa(s)\to k'$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. By step 1 (ii), $\bar s=\bar s'\circ a=(s,\alpha\circ\beta')$, so $\bar s$ lies over the same point $s$. Let $f:U\to S$ be an object of $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. By step 1 (i), a morphism $\bar u'=(u,\varphi'):\operatorname{Spec}k'\to U$ satisfies $f\circ\bar u'=\bar s'$ iff $f(u)=s$ and $\varphi'\circ r_u=\beta'$, where $r_u:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ is induced by $f$; likewise $\bar u=(u,\varphi):\operatorname{Spec}k\to U$ is a lift of $\bar s$ iff $f(u)=s$ and $\varphi\circ r_u=\alpha\circ\beta'$. So the pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar s'$ (resp. $\bar s$) [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods] with underlying $U$ are the triples $(U,u,\varphi')$ (resp. $(U,u,\varphi)$) as above, and the rule $\Phi:(U,\bar u')\mapsto(U,\bar u'\circ a)$ of the statement is $(U,u,\varphi')\mapsto(U,u,\alpha\circ\varphi')$ (step 1 (ii)); in particular $(U,\bar u'\circ a)$ is a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar s$, as the statement says.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Remark 04FN (remark-map-stalks, lines 3416-3441): 'the functor above is clearly an equivalence'; written out here

proof.text: ($\Phi$ is bijective on objects.) Fix $U$. Injectivity: $\alpha\circ\varphi'_1=\alpha\circ\varphi'_2$ implies $\varphi'_1=\varphi'_2$ since $\alpha$ is injective. Surjectivity: let $(U,u,\varphi)$ be a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar s$, so $f(u)=s$ and $\varphi\circ r_u=\alpha\circ\beta'$. Since $f$ is etale, $\kappa(u)$ is separable algebraic over $\kappa(s)$ through $r_u$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-residue-field-extension-separable], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $y\in\kappa(u)$ and let $P=\sum c_iT^i\in\kappa(s)[T]$ be nonzero with $\sum r_u(c_i)y^i=0$. Applying $\varphi$ gives $\sum\alpha(\beta'(c_i))\varphi(y)^i=0$, and the polynomial $\sum\alpha(\beta'(c_i))T^i$ has coefficients in $\alpha(k')$ and is nonzero ($\alpha\circ\beta'$ is injective). So $\varphi(y)$ is algebraic over $\alpha(k')$, and since $k'$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $\varphi(y)\in\alpha(k')$ by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-over-algebraically-closed-subfield]. Hence $\varphi(\kappa(u))\subseteq\alpha(k')$; as $\alpha:k'\to\alpha(k')$ is a bijective ring map, $\varphi':=\alpha^{-1}\circ\varphi:\kappa(u)\to k'$ is a field homomorphism with $\alpha\circ\varphi'=\varphi$, and $\alpha\circ(\varphi'\circ r_u)=\varphi\circ r_u=\alpha\circ\beta'$ gives $\varphi'\circ r_u=\beta'$ by injectivity of $\alpha$. So $(U,u,\varphi')$ is a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar s'$ with $\Phi(U,u,\varphi')=(U,u,\varphi)$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Remark 04FN (remark-map-stalks, lines 3416-3441): 'the functor above is clearly an equivalence'; written out here

proof.text: ($\Phi$ is an isomorphism of categories.) A morphism $(U,\bar u')\to(V,\bar v')$ of pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar s'$ is an $S$-morphism $h:U\to V$ with $h\circ\bar u'=\bar v'$; a morphism $(U,\bar u'\circ a)\to(V,\bar v'\circ a)$ of pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar s$ is an $S$-morphism $h$ with $h\circ\bar u'\circ a=\bar v'\circ a$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods]. By the injectivity of precomposition with $a$ (step 1 (ii), applied to $X=V$) the two conditions on $h$ are equivalent. Hence $\Phi$, defined on morphisms by $h\mapsto h$, is a functor that is bijective on every set of morphisms and (step 3) on objects: an isomorphism of categories $\mathcal N_{\bar s'}\to\mathcal N_{\bar s}$, compatible with the functors to $S_{\Et}$ forgetting the lift. (This is the equivalence asserted in Stacks 04FN, in the stronger form of an isomorphism.)

lean.statement:
theorem geometricPointMorphism_category_equivalence
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    [Field k'] [IsAlgClosed k'] (s : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S) (s' : Spec (.of k') ⟶ S)
    (a : Spec (.of k) ⟶ Spec (.of k')) (ha : a ≫ s' = s) :
    let b : Over.mk s ⟶ Over.mk s' := Over.homMk a ha
    let α : (pointSmallEtale s').fiber ⟶ (pointSmallEtale s).fiber :=
      Functor.whiskerLeft (Etale.forget S) (coyoneda.map b.op)
    (CategoryOfElements.map α).IsEquivalence
